text:
incident-bot: ALERT: SLO-API-5xx-rate above 2% for 5m in us-west-2. Paging primary: @alex_oncall. Related runbook: <https://kb.internal/redwood/runbooks/kv-cache-eviction>. Incident ID: INC-1998765432 :rotating_light:

alex_oncall: taking it. I'm about to hand off in ~20m so if this looks like it needs a longer suppression / threshold adjustment please call it out now. Checking dashboards...

alex_oncall: quick read — 5xxs are coming from our cache layer after the deploy to cache pool 7. Pattern looks like concurrent evictions causing a spike in origin requests. Impact: elevated 5xx on some routes, not a global outage.

sophie_eng: confirmed — saw same in canary logs. Root cause probably the new eviction heuristic. Runbook pointer: "KV cache eviction -> mitigation" in the link above. Steps I recommend: 1) apply suppression window to reduce paging noise, 2) revert heuristic or roll a hotfix if suppression doesn't reduce error amplification.

sophie_eng: command to set a temporal alert threshold (alert service):
```
alertctl update SLO-API-5xx-rate --threshold 3.0 --scope us-west-2 --expires 1998765600 --note "post-deploy cache thrash temporary threshold"
```

kevin_sre: prefer suppression over permanently changing SLO threshold. We should create a suppression window tied to the alert instead of muting the whole policy.

kevin_sre: suppression command (opsctl):
```
opsctl suppress --alert SLO-API-5xx-rate --until 1998765600 --reason "post-deploy cache thrash" --created-by alex_oncall
```

kevin_sre: also tagging the PD escalation policy to avoid 2am wakeups: `pdctl escalation update SLO-API-5xx-rate --snooze 40m`

julie_pm: any visible customer impact? Are payments / auth flows affected? We should notify CS if this touches >1% of sessions.

alex_oncall: current estimate from observability: ~120 requests/min returning 5xx across ~30 customers; user-facing session impact ~0.8% overall. No errors in billing path observed. If this stays >2.5% for 30m I will notify CS and notify sales ENG leads.

alex_oncall: summary & proposals:
- Apply suppression until 1998765600 (approx 11m from now) to stop paging churn.
- If errors drop to <1% within that window, roll forward with a small config tweak to eviction thresholds.
- If errors persist, roll back the eviction change and open an incident with SEV timeline.

alex_oncall: applying suppression now. I'll handoff primary to @kevin_sre at end of my shift (in 18m). Kevin, please take secondary after handoff and watch for regression during midnight window.

kevin_sre: ack — I'll take primary at handoff. If suppression expires and we see >2% again I'll trigger rollback and escalate.

sophie_eng: I'll prepare a quick rollback patch PR and keep it on standby. Link to PR in thread once created.

incident-bot: ACTION_LOG: suppression created for SLO-API-5xx-rate until 1998765600 by alex_oncall. Incident INC-1998765432 updated. PagerDuty: suppression applied, notifications muted for this alert.

alex_oncall: tagging runbook snippets here for handoff notes:
- KB: <https://kb.internal/redwood/runbooks/kv-cache-eviction>
- Quick rollback: `git rev-parse HEAD~1 && deploy rollback cache-service --target HEAD~1`
- Observability query (errors by route): `sum(rate(api_requests{status=~"5.."}[5m])) by (route)`

julie_pm: thanks. Please ping me if CS needs an official update.

alex_oncall: will do. doing a final check and then marking handoff in 15m. ty :thumbsup:

kevin_sre: noted. I'll monitor logs and the suppression expiry, and will extend suppression if we see transient noise but no service degradation.

incident-bot: NOTE: last_message_ts set to 1998765601 for record. This thread contains root alert + handoff coordination + suppression action.
